Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is carbamazepine, a neutral lipophilic low-MW tricyclic urea; the closest gold-context analog thalidomide showed probably high absolute oral bioavailability (80–100%) at low doses in fasting volunteers, supporting F ≥ 20%.

L4 direct intestinal absorption for the same dibenzazepine carboxamide scaffold: oxcarbazepine absorption was essentially complete after a single oral radiolabeled dose in healthy volunteers, supporting high intestinal absorption for carbamazepine.

L3 oral exposure records show measurable systemic exposure after oral dosing of carbamazepine-scaffold drugs: carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide AUC12 was 9.98 µg·h/mL after oral carbamazepine 200 mg BID, and fed-state Cmax of the eslicarbazepine metabolite was 12.8 µg/mL after oral eslicarbazepine acetate, indicating oral absorption is not impaired in the fed state.

L5 Caco-2 bidirectional records for neutral lipophilic aromatic amide/urea/heterocycle compounds show high passive permeability and low efflux ratios (ER ≈ 0.96–1.23), indicating no significant gut-wall efflux for this compound class; these are mechanistic, not direct carbamazepine F measurements.

L6 hepatic/metabolic records do not provide affirmative evidence of F < 20% for carbamazepine: BPCPU was metabolically stable in rat hepatocytes/microsomes (C76/C77/C74/C73), while oxcarbazepine AKR intrinsic-clearance and MHD glucuronidation records (C66/C71/C75) concern a different molecule/metabolite and do not establish low carbamazepine F; C69 only shows cimetidine increased epoxide half-life by 10–20%.
No affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F < 20%; low-dissolution record C46 is for an unrelated molecule (OIB) and is not used as evidence against carbamazepine.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for carbamazepine itself is supplied; C51 is oxcarbazepine absorption, not an F value.
No fed-state-specific F for carbamazepine; C32 is fed but for eslicarbazepine acetate metabolite exposure.
No direct carbamazepine Caco-2/efflux or intestinal metabolism record; L5 records are for other neutral lipophilic compounds.
L6 hepatic clearance records are mostly for other molecules (BPCPU, oxcarbazepine, cyproheptadine) or metabolite half-life; no direct carbamazepine hepatic clearance or first-pass quantification.
Several L5/L6 cards are duplicates or same-assay records and are not independent votes.
Low-solubility/dissolution records are for unrelated molecules and are not transferable.

L6 hepatic/metabolic records are mixed and mostly non-carbamazepine, providing no affirmative evidence for F < 20%; fed-state-specific direct F and carbamazepine-specific first-pass quantification remain gaps.
